# Line-based Histogram for 2D Scalar Pairs

Also called: Line-based boundary histogram

## Overview
A visualization method for displaying the 2D histogram of scalar value pairs $(S_1, S_2)$ sampled along the gradient direction, using lines instead of point primitives to make material boundaries intuitive [S1]. It differs from standard 2D histograms by mapping bin counts to line intensity and bin coordinates to axis positions, explicitly revealing the transition between two material types [S1].

## How it works
**Inputs:**
1. A precomputed 2D histogram $H$ of scalar pairs $(S_1, S_2)$, where $S_1$ is the scalar value in the gradient direction and $S_2$ is the scalar value opposite to the gradient direction [S1].
2. The dimensions of the histogram axes (number of bins for $S_1$ and $S_2$).

**Outputs:**
A 2D visualization where lines connect the top axis (representing $S_2$) to the bottom axis (representing $S_1$) [S1].

**Data Structures:**
The histogram $H$ is a 2D grid where each cell $H(i, j)$ corresponds to a bin pair. The value stored in $H(i, j)$ is the count of voxel pairs $(S_1, S_2)$ falling into those bins [S1].

**Steps:**
1. Define two parallel vertical axes. The bottom axis represents scalar values $S_1$ (gradient direction), increasing from left to right. The top axis represents scalar values $S_2$ (opposite to gradient direction) [S1].
2. For each bin $(i, j)$ in the 2D histogram where the count $H(i, j) > 0$:
   a. Determine the horizontal position $x_1$ on the bottom axis corresponding to bin $i$ (value $S_1$) [S1].
   b. Determine the horizontal position $x_2$ on the top axis corresponding to bin $j$ (value $S_2$) [S1].
   c. Draw a line segment connecting $(x_2, \text{top})$ to $(x_1, \text{bottom})$ [S1].
   d. Set the intensity (opacity or brightness) of the line proportional to the count $H(i, j)$ [S1].

**Interpretation:**
- Dense vertical lines indicate homogeneous regions where $S_1 \approx S_2$ [S1].
- Diagonal lines indicate boundaries between two different materials, with the start and end points indicating the scalar values of the respective materials [S1].

**Parameters:**
- Line intensity scaling factor: Not given in the sources.
- Axis resolution: Determined by the histogram bin count.

**Edge Cases:**
- If $H(i, j) = 0$, no line is drawn [S1].
- Precision issues in scalar sampling may affect bin assignment, but the method relies on the precomputed histogram [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Parallel Coordinate Plots Generation](9539-parallel-coordinate-plots-generation.md)
Each nonzero pixel P(i, j) in the joint histogram of attribute x and y yields a quad starting at position i on PC axis x and ending at position j on PC axis y.

## Operating characteristics
- **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of non-zero bins in the 2D histogram.
- **Memory Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of non-zero bins for storing line primitives.
- **Strengths:** Intuitively reveals material boundaries and homogeneous regions through line orientation and density [S1].
- **Limitations:** Requires precomputed 2D histogram; interpretation depends on understanding the gradient-aligned sampling context [S1].
- **When to use:** When the goal is to visualize material boundaries and transitions in scalar pairs for lighting transfer function specification [S1].
- **When not to use:** When detailed statistical distribution within bins is more important than boundary visualization [S1].

## Background
Originated in the paper "Lighting Transfer Functions Using Gradient Aligned Sampling" by [S1]. The method was developed to allow users to specify lighting for boundaries between materials by making boundary relationships immediately visible in the 2D histogram [S1].
